statement: ocentra-enforcer coordination MCP (both ocentra_enforcer_ and rust_rules_ aliases) refused writes as stale (package.json hash drift vs running server snapshot). Attempted documented fallback `node scripts/rust-rules.mjs coordination claim --json` and `coordination message --json` from C:\Projects\ocentra-enforcer (pack root, not worktree) -- both failed with ENOENT on .ledger/ocentra-parent/identity/node.json, i.e. the hub's own on-disk identity state is missing/uninitialized, not just a version mismatch.
why: Protocol says hub-down -> log+proceed; needed to confirm fallback CLI was also broken (not just MCP) before proceeding without claim/mail, so a later worker doesn't waste a retry cycle assuming the fallback works.
howToApply: If coordination_claim/coordination_mail MCP tools return writeCapable:false/stale, try the CLI fallback ONCE; if it errors ENOENT on .ledger/<hub>/identity/node.json, the whole coordination hub is uninitialized (not a staleness issue) -- log and proceed without claim/mail per protocol rather than retrying.

statement: enforcer_domain::findings::Finding has NO Tier field and no score/confidence fields -- Tier lives only on enforcer-rules::registry::RuleRecord (paired 1:1 with a RuleId), never per-Finding. So 'tag a Finding as Tier::T2/advisory' cannot mean setting a field on Finding; it means (1) picking a RuleId for the bridge (minted LIT-2.1, distinct from the per-category LIT-1.x ids already baked into enforcer-literal-scan's RiskCategory::rule_id()), and (2) NEVER constructing that Finding with Severity::Error -- Violation::try_from(Finding) is the ONLY path to a blocking Violation and it hard-fails unless severity==Error, so Severity::Warning/Info is what makes non-blocking structurally true, not a tier tag.
why: A worker reading only Finding's field list would look for a tier/advisory boolean that does not exist and either invent one (schema drift) or wrongly conclude the bridge needs to modify enforcer-domain. The actual non-blocking mechanism is a SEVERITY discipline enforced by a separate TryFrom guard on Violation, not a Finding-level flag.
howToApply: When a workpack says 'tag a Finding as T2/advisory/non-blocking', grep enforcer-domain/src/findings.rs for Violation::try_from first -- if it gate-checks severity==Error (it does, as of this build), then 'advisory' is fully satisfied by always emitting Severity::Warning or Severity::Info from your Validator, never Severity::Error. No Tier plumbing on Finding is needed or exists.

statement: enforcer-literal-scan's only public scan entry point (run_scan) is filesystem-rooted (reads via CliOptions.root/.files, walks + fs::read_to_string internally) and therefore CANNOT be called from inside a Validator::validate impl, whose ValidationInput contract is pure-in-memory (file: &RelPath, source: &str, no I/O). The crate already has the pure primitives needed to build a Validator without touching run_scan: pub(crate) detect_language(path, include_unknown) -> Option<LanguageSpec>, pub(crate) classify_file_role(rel, language) -> FileRole, pub(crate) lex_literals(source, language, rel) -> Vec<LiteralCandidate> (crate::lexer), and pub(crate) classify_literal(candidate, file, language_id, role, repeated_files, fail_above) -> crate's own Finding (crate::risk) -- all four are pure over &str/candidate data with zero fs access, and all are pub(crate) so a same-crate bridge.rs module can call them directly without changing any visibility.
why: The obvious-looking shortcut (write ValidationInput.source to a temp file, call run_scan) would violate the Validator trait's own documented purity invariant (same input -> same output, no hidden I/O) that the fixture/parity harness in enforcer-validator relies on, and would also silently drop the per-file 'role' classification signal that run_scan derives from the REAL path, not a temp path.
howToApply: Before bridging any existing scan/CLI-shaped crate into the Validator trait, do NOT assume the crate's top-level pub run_* entry point is usable -- grep its lib.rs for pub(crate) exports of the smaller per-file pure functions the top-level entry point composes internally (discovery/lexer/risk-scoring granularity), and build the bridge directly on those, bypassing the filesystem-walking outer function entirely.

statement: e01 completed and pushed lane/e01 (commit f1f02bb feat + bd9b81f-rebased chore(e01) lock regen, final rebased head after two additional rebase cycles onto origin/rust-build which moved from d17->d04->d05 mid-session) without ever successfully claiming lane e01 or sending a started/closeout mail via the coordination hub -- both ocentra_enforcer_*/rust_rules_* MCP tools and the scripts/rust-rules.mjs CLI fallback failed identically (ENOENT .ledger/ocentra-parent/identity/node.json) at session start, mid-pack, and closeout.
why: Confirms the hub-down condition was persistent for the whole session duration (not transient), and that per-protocol hub-down fallback (log+proceed) was the correct and only viable path for this lane; a later worker or the orchestrator repairing the hub should know e01's work landed via git push alone, with no coordination-ledger record of the claim/lifecycle.
howToApply: If you are the orchestrator or a hub-repair task: lane/e01 pushed clean work (universal literal-scan T2 bridge, LIT-2.1) with zero ledger claim/mail events for the whole session -- do not treat the absence of e01 ledger events as evidence the work didn't happen; check git log on origin/lane/e01 instead.
